t: I think you remember that in Kolkata a few days ago I said, Saḿgráme vaepariityaḿ – “When in battle, one should take the help of an opposite thought.” Similarly, to save oneself from dark spots and filth inside the human mind, it is necessary to take an opposite thought. Suppose someone is making progress. Seeing this, someone elseʼs mind starts burning with jealousy. To stave this off, what thought should be taken? “That person is my friend. He/she is making progress. It is a matter of joy.” That is, you are taking the opposite thought.

If one sees someone doing some good deed, oneʼs mind should not burn. If that does happen, it must be rectified. To do that, the person [who does the good deed] should be encouraged. One should say “Yes, brother or sister, you are doing very good work.” This is the policy. Human beings have defects and weaknesses, and to banish them, an opposite thought should be taken. This will calm down the mind. The physical body will remain free from diseases. Human beings have many flaws. Of these, one big flaw is ego – the desire to be honoured. Another flaw is slandering others, gossiping. Slandering others and gossiping are mouth-watering “foods”. Once started, slandering others continues hour after hour.There should be some means to save oneself from all these things. The scriptures say:
Abhimánaḿ surápánaḿ
Gaoravaḿ raoravaḿ dhruvam,
Pratiśt́há shúkariiviśt́há
Trayaḿ tyaktvá Hariḿ bhajet.

[Abhimána is like surápána, gaorava leads to raorava, and pratiśt́há is like shúkariiviśt́há: an inflated ego is like drinking wine, self-aggrandizement leads one into the deepest hell, and social status is like the excrement of a pig.]

Wounded pride stems from the desire to have honour, to have respect. How can we describe it? Drinking alcohol is a bad habit. [Defending oneʼs] pride is as bad as that bad habit. You may ask, why do we call drinking alcohol, in particular, a bad habit? Drinking coffee or cocoa, or chewing betel leaf – all these things are bad actions. Why is so much being said about wine? The answer is this: That which destroys the naturalness of the brainʼs functioning is the most harmful thing. The most valuable wealth of humans is their intellect. Human beings are intellectual creatures. If a person drinks alcohol, the intellect is completely destroyed. Out of all addictive things, the worst one is alcohol. And pride, that is, the yearning to be honoured by others, is as bad as drinking alcohol. That is, just as if people drink, they will undergo intellectual and spiritual degradation, so also the desire to be honoured by others is the cause of degradation. Humans will have to save themselves from these vices.

So in battle, we will have to have recourse to the opposite thought. Therefore when the mind starts desiring to be honoured – “Let people pay selám [salaam], namaskára to me” – what should then be done? You will have to give respect and honour to others. This will create the opposite thought, and the mind will become calm. Suppose a question arises in your mind why a certain person did not do namaskára. As soon as such a thought grips the mind, do namaskára immediately – the mind will become calm. I have said that I will call a gentleman one who always does namaskára first, rather than doing it in return. [Some peopleʼs attitude is] if anyone does namaskára to you before you do it, only then will you do namaskára to that person in return. But if you do namaskára before the person does, it is that person who will have to return the namaskára. So, one is a gentleman who does namaskára first – not the person who does namaskára in return.

Where there is a craving to get respect, what to do? Trńád api suniicena – Think yourself to be “equal to a blade of grass.” You know that the modesty within a person does not make him/her small. Modesty makes a person great, not small. You will notice one thing. A baby is sitting on the lap of the mother. The lap of the mother is under the feet of the baby. The mother lies under the feet of her baby. And the baby is seated on the lap of its mother. Does it mean that the mother has become small? No – Mother Earth is under everyoneʼs feet. Does it mean that respect for Mother Earth evaporates? No, it rather increases her honour. So follow the example of a blade of grass, be like a blade of grass. This will make you great, not small. When you desire to get honour, take the ideation Trńád api suniicena. Here suniicena [literally, “lower”] has been said, not niicena [“equally low”]. That is, this kind of becoming small is a matter of glory, a matter of bliss. In this way honour is increased, not decreased.

Taror iva sahiśńuná. Taru means “tree”. Be tolerant like trees. Even when humans are cutting a tree, the tree continues to provide shade for them, it does not deprive them of shade. Like a tree, like a taru, be tolerant.

Here you should remember one thing. Tolerance is a noble virtue in individual life. But is it in collective life as well? No. In individual life, forgive and tolerate as much as possible. Forgiveness and tolerance are certainly great virtues in individual life. But remember, in collective life you have no right to forgive. Suppose someone strikes you a blow in collective life. In that case, you have no right to forgive or tolerate. Because this is not just your individual matter, it is a collective matter. So, instead of forgiving and tolerating, engage in conflict with the attackers. Strike back against the enemy, remove him/her, drive him/her away – do not show tolerance, do not forgive, because it is a matter of collective life. But if anyone strikes you a blow in individual life, you can be as forgiving as possible, as tolerant as possible.

Forgiveness is a noble virtue in individual life. It is a great demerit in collective life. Indians are affected with this demerit in collective life. So remain alert. This demerit is extremely bad. Because of this demerit, there has been degradation in collective life.

Suppose no one in society pays honour or respect to a person. What will you do? You will pay honour to the person. Suppose no one invites a person, “Please come and sit.” What will you tell the person? “Please come, kindly take your seat.” Suppose there is a person to whom no one does namaskára. Do namaskára to the person. You will see one thing. Your mind will become pure and sanctified. If instead of a yearning in the mind to get something, there is a yearning to give something, the mind will become pure. Yesterday evening, one thing was said: Vaekuńt́ha gets established in a pure heart. So you will pay honour to a person to whom no one pays honour. Do remember one thing. An idle brain is the devilʼs workshop. If there is no work to do, humans will surely commit misdeeds. The mind cannot remain stationary. It will remain engaged in some kind of work. When you realize that you cannot give it its pabulum, you cannot give it its food, what will you do under such circumstances? Kiirttaniyah sadá Harih. Without wasting time, do kiirtana immediately. Gather two or four, five or six persons. Start doing Harikiirtana collectively. In this way there will be no degradation of the mind, rather there will be progress. For this reason, Kiirttaniyah sadá Harih – “Do Harikiirtana all the time.”

You will have to do kiirtana. The kiirtana of whom? The kiirtana of Parama Puruśa. Parama Puruśa has thousands and hundreds of thousands of names. He has limitless attributes, and therefore He has limitless names. But Parama Puruśa has one name that is for everyone – Hari. For every spiritual aspirant, for purposes of doing kiirtana there is just one name – not many. Parama Puruśa is called Hari for this reason: with Parama Puruśa you have an individual, familial relationship. In a family, parents love their children. They chide them if they commit misdeed. This is because the relationship is one of love. This is not the relationship between the judge and the criminal. It is a completely personal and familial relationship. Many people say that Parama Puruśa is a judge. No, the role of Parama Puruśa is not that of a judge. He admonishes because there is a personal and familial relationship. Why should Parama Puruśa be a judge? A judge is a thing of the mundane world. In the mundane world, if anyone does an unjust action, society will try to punish the person. But in the spiritual sphere, Parama Puruśa will take those who are devotees of the Supreme Consciousness onto His lap and make them sit. The judiciary should be for ordinary human beings. To keep society clean, the doer of illegal deeds must be punished. But if, because of a relationship of love, Parama Puruśa tells anyone, “Oh, my devotee, kindly give me all your sins,” the devotee will never oblige Him. Rather the devotee will say, “I will give you flowers, foods, sweets, but how can I give you my sins? I wonʼt do it.” So a devotee will not give sins.

But a devotee is extremely dear to Parama Puruśa. For this reason, Parama Puruśa takes away that personʼs sins stealthily. Yes, Parama Puruśa does steal the sins of devotees. That is why one of His names is Hari. So it has been said, Kiirttaniyah sadá Harih – always do Harikiirtana.

When people remain immersed in doing Harikiirtana, there is no mental degradation. Rather, the mind remains pure, holy and healthy. Spiritual practice is speeded up; therefore every spiritual aspirant, when they get some free time, should do Harikiirtana collectively with two or four or ten persons. Thus you will keep your mind free of stains so that you can make more and more progress in your spiritual practice.
Ánanda Vacanámrtam Part 28 [unpublished in English]
The Flow of Devotion and the Glory of Kiirtana [a compilation]
I have told you several times:
Trńád api suniicena taror iva sahiśńuná,
Amáninaḿ mána deyaḿ kiirttaniiyah sadá harih.
[You must be more humble than the grass and more tolerant than the trees. You must give respect to those whom no one respects, and always do kiirtana to the Lord.]

Perhaps you have noticed one thing. Many people think themselves to be superior to others. This kind of thought should be shunned. Again, some think themselves to be inferior to others. Why do they think so? There are three reasons behind it: First, because of lack of education, a kind of inferiority complex awakens inside human beings; second, because of so-called casteism; third, because of poverty.

Remember, no one is either inferior or superior to anyone on this earth. All are equal as the children of Parama Puruśa. Make arrangements for the proper education of those who have not been able to get educated. Keep an eye out so that there is no division with regard to casteism.

All are the same “caste”, and that is the human “caste”. All will have to make efforts collectively for the economic self-sufficiency of those who are economically undeveloped. Thus a feeling of equality wiil have to be awakened in all. Suppose there is a person whom no one honours. All will have to endeavour so that the person becomes worthy of earning honour.

You will have to remember one thing. You will have to acquire the capacity to endure everything. But you will endure only to accumulate strength. If a person attacks you, you have to apply force to resist the attack. But if you do, your force will be misused as a result. What should you do in that case? To [counter-]attack, you have to apply a certain amount of force. Instead, applying less force, preserve the force used by the attacker. Thereafter, combining your own force with the preserved force, you are to repulse the attacker. Suppose, one has aimed an arrow at you. To resist the strike of the arrow, it is necessary to apply an opposite force. But rather than doing that, catch the arrow by applying a smaller amount of force. Thereafter, apply the arrowʼs force [not the arrow] against the attacker. To do this, you must enhance your tolerance. Because taror iva sahiśńuná – I am saying again, do not tolerate only for the sake of tolerance. Tolerate for the sake of counter-attacking.

And again, kiirttaniyah sadá Harih. Whenever you have free time, do His kiirtana, taking His name. If Hari exists, then you belong to Him. To Him, no one is either superior to you or inferior to you. All are equal. Therefore, whenever you will all have time, do His kiirtana collectively. If you do kiirtana, your mind will become pure. The speed of spiritual practice will be accelerated, and you will acquire force.
Ánanda Vacanámrtam Part 28 [unpublished in English]
The Flow of Devotion and the Glory of Kiirtana [a compilation]
